title: The Docker CLI Unlocked 🔑
description: Master the structure of Docker commands and learn how to find help on your own.

slides.title: The Anatomy of a Docker Command 🧬
slides.content:
# How Docker Commands Are Structured

Every Docker command follows this pattern:

```
docker <management‑command> <subcommand> [OPTIONS] [ARGUMENTS]
```

- **docker** – the client program
- **management‑command** – a group of related operations (e.g., `image`, `container`, `volume`, `network`)
- **subcommand** – the action you want to perform (e.g., `ls`, `rm`, `inspect`)
- **OPTIONS** – flags that modify behaviour (e.g., `-a`, `--format`, `--filter`)
- **ARGUMENTS** – the target object (e.g., image name, container ID)

**Example:**
```bash
docker container ls -a
```
- management command: `container`
- subcommand: `ls` (list)
- option: `-a` (show all containers)

slides.title: Old‑Style vs New‑Style Commands 🕰️
slides.content:
## Shorthand or Management Commands?
Docker supports two styles:

| Old style          | New style                 |
|-------------------|---------------------------|
| `docker ps`       | `docker container ls`     |
| `docker images`   | `docker image ls`        |
| `docker rm`       | `docker container rm`    |
| `docker rmi`      | `docker image rm`        |

Both work. The new style is more consistent and descriptive. We’ll use both so you’re comfortable everywhere.

quizData.question: In the command `docker image ls -a`, what is `-a`?
quizData.explanation: `-a` is an option (flag) that modifies the behaviour of the `ls` subcommand.

slides.title: Getting Help from the CLI 🆘
slides.content: Docker has built‑in help that you should use constantly:
slides.codeSnippet:
# List all top‑level commands
docker --help

# Get help on a specific management command
docker container --help

# Get help on a subcommand
docker container run --help

quizData.question: Which command shows you all available options for `docker run`?
quizData.explanation: The `--help` flag works on any command and subcommand. It’s the fastest way to learn what a command can do.

slides.title: Command Categories at a Glance 📋
slides.content:
# Most Important Docker Commands

**Containers**
- `docker container ls` / `docker ps`
- `docker container run`
- `docker container stop`
- `docker container rm`

**Images**
- `docker image ls` / `docker images`
- `docker image pull`
- `docker image rm` / `docker rmi`

**System**
- `docker version`
- `docker info`
- `docker system prune`

You’ll master each of these throughout this course!
